title: Will They Talk: Offered and Requested Quality of Service, and the Silence When They Do Not Match

questions.question: A camera driver publishes best effort and a node subscribes with the default profile, reliable. What happens?
options: Images arrive, but some are missing, because best effort does not resend
They are never connected, nothing is delivered, and the only report is a warning in a log: the most common cause of a subscriber that gets no data
The subscriber is downgraded to best effort without a word and images arrive
The publisher is upgraded to reliable and slows down to acknowledge each image
questions.explanation: The offer must be at least as strong as the request. A publisher that sends once cannot promise delivery, so the two are never connected.

questions.question: Is the compatibility rule symmetric?
options: No: a reliable offer meets either request and a best effort offer only best effort, so the order of offer and request matters
Yes: any two profiles that share a reliability setting are connected
Yes for reliability, and no only for the deadline
No: a best effort offer meets either request and a reliable offer only reliable
questions.explanation: Reliable delivery includes best effort, so a stronger offer serves a weaker request. The other way round has nothing to give.

questions.question: An offer of a message every 0.5 s meets which request?
options: One for every 0.1 s, since the publisher is at least that fast
Only one for exactly 0.5 s
Any request at all: a publisher with a deadline meets every subscriber
One for every 0.5 s or longer, or no deadline at all, but not every 0.1 s
questions.explanation: The deadline is the longest gap. A promise of a message within 0.5 s satisfies anyone who needs one within 0.5 s or more, and not someone who needs one within 0.1 s.

questions.question: A subscriber requests a deadline and the publisher offers none. Compatible?
options: Yes: a publisher with no deadline is free to meet any
Yes, as long as the publisher is reliable
No: silence is not a promise, so a demand cannot be met by offering nothing
It depends on how fast the publisher happens to send
questions.explanation: Offering no deadline is making no promise. A subscriber that asks for none is satisfied by anything; one that asks for one needs it promised.

questions.question: Why does the check name each property that does not fit?
options: The middleware requires a reason string for every refusal
So that the check can be repeated for each property in turn
Because a yes or no cannot be logged
A yes or no leaves a person guessing which of five properties differed: the camera against the demanding node gave three named reasons
questions.explanation: The camera against the demanding node differed in reliability, durability and deadline. Named, each is a line to change; unnamed, it is a guessing game.

questions.question: What did the matcher do with the detector, subscribing with the default profile to the camera's image?
options: Did not connect it and reported one reason, reliability, while the best effort viewer was connected
Connected it, and delivered images with gaps
Connected it after changing the detector's request to best effort
Refused the camera, so the viewer lost its images as well
questions.explanation: The detector asked for reliable and the camera offers best effort. The viewer asked for best effort and was connected, which is why the camera looks fine from elsewhere.
